h1: Solar Detach & Reset in Johnstown, CO
heroSub: Johnstown roofs are newer than most, but northern Colorado hail doesn't care. We take your panels down so your roofer can do the job right, then reset them and confirm the system is producing before we leave.
introHtml:
Johnstown has grown fast along the I-25 and US 34 corridor, and a big share of those new rooftops came with solar already on them, either sold with the house or on a lease the buyer inherited at closing. Hail doesn't check the build date, so plenty of Johnstown homes under ten years old are already working through their first storm claim. When the roof gets approved for replacement, the panels have to come off first, and most roofers won't touch them.

That's the job we do. Greeley Solar Reset handles solar detach and reset all over Johnstown, from the older blocks near downtown to the big subdivisions on both sides of I-25. We photograph and map the system, pull it down safely, store or stage the panels, and reinstall everything on the new roof with fresh flashing and a full system check. Every job starts with a free written estimate, which is exactly the line item your insurance scope needs. Call (970) 286-3417 and we'll get on the schedule alongside your roofer.

sections.heading: Why Johnstown Roofs Are Filing Hail Claims So Young
sections.html:
Johnstown sits squarely in one of the most active hail corridors in the country. The subdivisions that filled in around the I-25 and US 34 interchange and out along Highway 60 are mostly new builds, but a roof installed five years ago has still eaten five northern Colorado hail seasons. Adjusters total young roofs here all the time, and if there's solar on top, the detach and reset belongs in that same claim.

The good news is that insurance scopes routinely include solar detach and reset as a covered line item once the roof replacement is approved. The trap is letting that number show up late, after the scope is written, and getting stuck chasing a supplement. We give you a free written estimate early so the figure is in front of the adjuster from the start. Our removal and reinstall cost guide breaks down what drives the price.

One more Johnstown wrinkle: the town straddles the Weld and Larimer county line at I-25, so permitting can differ depending on which side of the highway you're on. We've worked both sides of the line and coordinate with your roofer so nothing stalls at the permit desk.

sections.heading: When Your Solar Came With the House
sections.html:
In a lot of Johnstown neighborhoods, solar wasn't something the homeowner shopped for. It came bundled with the new build, or it transferred with a lease or power purchase agreement when the house sold. That means many owners facing a reroof have never dealt with their solar company at all, and the first call after a hailstorm can get confusing fast.

Here's the practical version. If you own the panels outright, you can hire anyone qualified to detach and reset them. If they're leased or third-party owned, the agreement usually spells out how removal has to be handled, and some companies quote long lead times right when your roofer is ready to start. We help you read what your agreement actually requires, do the work to those standards, and keep photo and serial-number documentation so there's never a question about the system's condition before and after.

Either way, don't let anyone talk you into roofing around the array or leaving panels stacked in the garage indefinitely. A proper detach protects the equipment, the roof warranty, and your production numbers, and if you're unwinding a lease entirely, our panel removal service covers full takedowns too.

sections.heading: How Detach and Reset Works for Johnstown Homes
sections.html:
It starts with a site visit and a free written estimate. We document the array layout, wiring, and racking, note any existing hail damage, and lock our detach date to your roofer's tear-off date. On a typical Johnstown house the detach takes a few hours, and most residential arrays come off in a single morning.

While your roofer works, the panels are stored safely or staged on site where they can't be damaged. Once the new roof passes inspection, we come back, install new flashing at every penetration, torque the racking to spec, reconnect the system, and verify it's producing before we leave. You get before-and-after photos and a completion record for your insurance file.

Plan on a few days to about a week with the panels off, depending on your roofer's schedule and inspection timing. If a storm hits mid-project, our 24/7 emergency line at (970) 286-3417 covers you, day or night.

faq.q: My Johnstown house came with solar I don't own. Can you still detach and reset it?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Most leases and power purchase agreements allow a licensed, insured third party to do the detach and reset, though some require you to notify the leasing company first or use an approved contractor. Call them early in your reroof planning, and we'll handle whatever paperwork they need so your roofer isn't left waiting.

faq.q: How much does solar detach and reset cost in Johnstown?
faq.a: Most residential jobs in Johnstown land between $2,500 and $5,500 depending on how many panels you have, roof height, and pitch. That usually works out to roughly $150 to $300 per panel for the full detach and reset. If the reroof is a hail claim, insurance typically covers this as a line item, and our written estimate is free either way.

faq.q: My roof is only a few years old. Will insurance really pay for detach and reset?
faq.a: If the adjuster approves the roof replacement, the detach and reset is normally covered in that same claim, regardless of roof age. Johnstown gets enough hail that young roofs total out all the time. Check your scope for the line item, and if it's missing, our itemized written estimate gives your roofer what they need to file a supplement.

faq.q: Johnstown sits in both Weld and Larimer counties. Does that change anything for my project?
faq.a: It can change which building department issues the reroof permit and runs inspections, and timelines differ a little between offices. It doesn't change our work. We coordinate permit timing with your roofer on either side of I-25 so the panels come down and go back up without dead days in between.
